keyframe_review.note: New keyframe, -1077..-1001: the Tanis dynasty's own land, the Delta. 'The pharaohs of the Twenty-first Dynasty ruled from Tanis, but were mostly active only in Lower Egypt, which they controlled'; 'Meanwhile, the High Priests of Amun at Thebes effectively ruled Middle and Upper Egypt in all but name.' Cliopatria's New Kingdom shapes cover -1150..-1001 with Egypt, Nubia and Israel (see the New Kingdom dossier's -1150 verdict). The page gives no area. [Reviewer me-03-b, 2026-10-18] The spec now includes the priests' land, as its text says and as keyframe new-kingdom-of-egypt_-1000 does ('Lower Egypt direct, Middle and Upper Egypt as the Theban priests' vassal tint'), so the two keyframes agree; it was the Delta alone.

correction.text: the Egypt outline as drawn, for -1000..-944: Lower Egypt direct, Middle and Upper Egypt as the Theban priests' vassal tint

keyframe_review.note: -1000..-901, 340,593 km2, bbox 23.5-31.7 N: Aswan to the Mediterranean. Right as the outline of Egypt but not as one state's direct territory: until 943 the Delta is the Tanis dynasty's and 'Middle and Upper Egypt' the Theban priests' 'in all but name'; from 943 it is the Twenty-second Dynasty's years (see that dossier). The shape also spans 943, 57 years of this state and 43 of the next. No area on the page for comparison.

ledger.note: 1077: Smendes founds the Twenty-first Dynasty at Tanis. Infobox 'Established: 1077 BC'; Smendes (1077-1051) 'Only controlled Lower Egypt during his reign'; the Third Intermediate Period began 'with the death of Pharaoh Ramesses XI in 1077 BC'.

region.text: Middle and Upper Egypt under the High Priests of Amun at Thebes

ledger.note: 1077: the Theban priests rule the south. 'The High Priests of Amun at Thebes effectively ruled Middle and Upper Egypt in all but name.' Drawn as vassal tint because the page says they ruled 'in all but name', i.e. under the Tanis kings' nominal rule; the page gives no tribute or oath, so the status is the researcher's reading.
943: the dynasty ends and with it its nominal overlordship of Thebes. The 22nd Dynasty page does not say whether Shoshenq I held the south (page silent).

region.text: the Delta, passing to the Twenty-second Dynasty

ledger.note: 943: the Twenty-first Dynasty gives way to Shoshenq I's Twenty-second. Infobox 'Disestablished: 943 BC', 'Succeeded by Twenty-second Dynasty of Egypt'; Psusennes II 966-943 BC. The Third Intermediate Period page gives the 22nd Dynasty's foundation as 945 BC (or 943 BC).

certainty.note: The line between the Tanis kings' Delta and the priests' south is not given on any page opened.

notes:
New state split from the Cliopatria row 'New Kingdom of Egypt' (-1500..-801): this dossier reviews shape -1000 (its years -1000..-944) and adds a new keyframe for -1077..-1001, which Cliopatria's -1150 shape (Egypt, Nubia, Israel) draws instead. Shape -900 is reviewed in twenty-second-dynasty-of-egypt.
The High Priests of Amun at Thebes (Middle and Upper Egypt, 1077-943) need their own dossier or a decision that they are part of this state: counterpart 'high-priests-of-amun-at-thebes'. The pages opened (21st Dynasty, Third Intermediate Period, New Kingdom) give no dates for their rulers (Herihor, Pinedjem) or for the relation to Tanis; a gap-filler should open the 'High Priest of Amun' and 'Siamun' pages.
Not covered by the pages opened: Nubia and Canaan in this period (Siamun's campaign, Kush's independence: the Kingdom of Kush page gives c. 1070 BC and is cited in the New Kingdom dossier), Shoshenq I's reunification and Levantine campaign (22nd Dynasty page silent). No war is named on the 21st Dynasty or Third Intermediate Period pages.
The king table overlaps (Psusennes I 1047-998, Amenemope 1000-991); the rulers strip follows the page with the overlaps trimmed by one year. No area figure on any page opened.
